intent: Detect the target JDK and add the cacheType option
resolve the target JDK and the cache type

title: probe the target JDK by running its own java -XshowSettings:properties -version
why: An archive is bound to the JDK of the application, and that JDK can differ from the JDK that runs the tool (issue 2). Asking the target java binary for its properties returns the vendor and full build as that JVM reports them. The probe has a 30 second timeout.
alternative: Read the release file in the Java home. Issue 2 names it as an option. No reason for rejecting it is recorded.

title: resolve the target JDK from --java-home, then JAVA_HOME, then the running JVM
why: An explicit choice by the user wins. The environment variable comes next. The JVM that runs the tool is the last resort. PR 25 describes this order; no other order is recorded.
alternative: Unknown. Searching the PATH for java is not implemented and no reason is recorded.

title: use the AOT cache only from JDK 25; JDK 24 stays on AppCDS
why: The single-step flag -XX:AOTCacheOutput works from JDK 25 (JEP 514). It was checked on JDK 25.0.1 in this project. JDK 24 has the AOT cache only through a two-step record and create flow, and supporting two AOT flows was not worth it before users ask. This threshold was corrected in a direct commit before PR 25 and PR 25 builds on it.
alternative: Implement the JDK 24 two-step flow (-XX:AOTMode=record, then create). Deferred and tracked as issue 22.

title: keep the user request (CacheType) apart from the resolved mechanism (CacheStrategy)
why: The request auto, appcds or aot can become JVM flags only after the JDK is known. Keeping them apart means that forcing aot on a JDK older than 25 is a clear error that names the required version, and auto never downgrades silently.
alternative: One enum with the JDK check inside. The PR does not record this as considered, so the alternative is unknown.

name: JdkInfo
role: Facts about the target JDK: Java home, version, feature release, vendor and full build
conditions: Needs a runnable bin/java under the Java home. Version strings such as 1.8.0_292 and 25-ea are parsed to feature releases 8 and 25

name: CacheStrategy
role: The resolved mechanism, AppCDS (.jsa) or Leyden AOT (.aot), with the training flag and the runtime flag for each
conditions: AOT flags need JDK 25 or later

name: CacheType
role: The user request auto, appcds or aot, resolved against a JDK
conditions: Forcing aot on a JDK older than 25 throws IllegalArgumentException that names JDK 25; auto picks AOT on 25 or later and AppCDS otherwise

name: build command (CLI)
role: picocli command that reports the target JDK and the chosen cache; options --java-home and --cache-type

subject: Feature release drives the choice
why: Cache selection uses the feature release (21, 25), not the full version string. Legacy and early-access strings are normalised first, so 1.8.0_292 means 8 and 25-ea means 25.

title: keep the user request (CacheType) apart from the resolved mechanism (CacheStrategy)
why: The request auto, appcds or aot can become JVM flags only after the JDK is known. Keeping the request apart from the result means a forced aot on a JDK older than 25 is a clear error that names the required version, instead of a wrong flag. Auto choosing AppCDS on older JDKs is intended, not a fallback.
alternative: One enum with the JDK check inside. The PR does not record this as considered, so the alternative is unknown.
